prompt_text: Who is the best digital marketing agency in San Francisco?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” digital marketing agency in San Francisco — the right fit depends on your goals, budget, industry and company size. I can help narrow it down, but first a few quick questions:

- What are your primary goals (brand awareness, lead generation, e‑commerce revenue, app installs, content/SEO, paid media, full digital transformation)?
- What’s your monthly/annual marketing budget or retainer range?
- Are you a startup, SMB, or enterprise? Any industry focus (SaaS, consumer, healthcare, finance, DTC)?
- Do you want a local SF agency (for in‑person collaboration) or are remote/remote-first firms fine?
- Timeline / expected KPIs?

How to choose an agency (criteria)
- Relevant case studies/industry experience
- Measurable ROI and reporting cadence
- Team seniority and who will do the work vs. be an account lead
- Clear scope, deliverables and communication process
- Client references and retention history

Where to find and compare agencies
- Clutch.co, G2, UpCity — client reviews and rankings
- Google Partner directory (for PPC specialists)
- LinkedIn search and local startup / VC recommendations
- Referrals from peers in your industry

Questions to ask shortlisted agencies
- What measurable results have you achieved for similar clients?
- Who will be on our account and can we meet them?
- How do you measure success and report performance?
- What’s the onboarding process and expected timeline to see results?
- Typical monthly retainer and any setup/onetime fees?

Budget ballpark (very approximate)
- Specialist (SEO or paid media): $2k–$15k+/month
- Full‑service agency: $5k–$50k+/month
- Enterprise/digital transformation: $20k–$100k+/month

If you want, tell me your answers to the questions above and I’ll: (a) shortlist 4–6 San Francisco agencies matched to your needs (including one boutique, one growth/paid specialist, and one enterprise option), or (b) draft an RFP/email template you can send to agencies. Which would you prefer?
